newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean worker defects, arrives in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean worker defects, arrives in Seoul.

text.p: A North Korean construction worker who had sought political asylum at a South Korean mission in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) arrived in Seoul on Tuesday, the South Korean foreign ministry said.
The application by Kim Kyung-chul, 44, for political asylum had been accepted by the Seoul government on humanitarian grounds, a ministry spokesman said.
He did not name the country and said the government had decided not to disclose details on North Korean defectors in order to protect their families.
Many North Korean escapees in the South use false names to protect themselves from attacks and to protect their family members, who are often sent to political gulags or sometimes executed.
Kim's arrival in Seoul followed the defection on Sunday of a 38-year-old North Korean civilian who escaped to the South through the heavily fortified border between the two countries.
The two Koreas remain technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended with a truce rather than a peace agreement.
A food shortage in Stalinist North Korea has led to a string of defections into the capitalist South. The Seoul government is building a camp south of Seoul to house up to 500 North Korean escapees.
